Out of the five Invicta Pro Diver automatic watches I’ve bought from Amazon, only one arrived with no significant problem. The first two watches were accurate enough when stored but lost time at a rate of one to six minutes a day when worn on the wrist. The third watch had acceptable accuracy but the rotating bezel was incredibly loose, horizontally and vertically. I didn’t notice how bad the bezel was until the 30-day return period elapsed. I “fixed” the problem by wrapping four turns of waxed dental floss under the bezel. Not an ideal solution, but it works, at least for now.This black dial/bezel model 8926OB is an attractive watch and is the second most accurate of the five Invicta Pro Diver automatic watches I’ve owned. When stored dial up, it gained time at the rate of a few seconds a day. When worn on the wrist, it usually lost time at a rate of ten seconds or so a day. This is excellent for an inexpensive automatic watch. There are much more expensive automatic watches which aren’t this accurate.However, I returned this watch because the rotating bezel was extremely loose. The bezel didn't have the excess vertical play another Pro Diver did, but the horizontal play was awful. Just lightly touching the bezel with a finger tip moved it a quarter inch. Because this watch’s accuracy was so good, I was tempted to try the dental floss “fix” and keep the watch but finally decided against it.I can’t comment on the bracelet as the first thing I do with Invicta watches is replace the cheap metal bracelet with a high quality NATO nylon strap. The lume on Invicta watches is mediocre but you can’t expect much better considering the price.My advice concerning Invicta Pro Diver automatic watches: Only buy them on Amazon when they’re on sale. When the watch arrives, inspect it closely, especially the bezel and screw-down crown. Besides two loose bezels, one of the Pro Divers I received had a very gritty screw-down crown. Either manually or with an app, carefully check the watch’s accuracy. Be sure and check the watch’s accuracy when worn on your wrist, not just stored. Check the watch for scratches or other blemishes. Invicta’s quality control is pretty bad and their warranty is virtually worthless. You need to examine and test the watch thoroughly within Amazon's 30-day return period.

The case is more polished than the description and though the inscription on the side (admittedly) is an eyesore, it still is a very good-looking watch that succeeds in capturing the look of the Submariner.However, the crown, a screwdown, did not want to close after I set the time. It get it to close, it really requires you to push down hard as you're screwing. Even then, the threads are difficult to catch. It seems like something that is destined to break before long.The clasp is also difficult to open and close. Perhaps it would become easier with repeated use, but in general it feels flimsy.

For value I rate this watch four stars. For daily wear or durability I rate it three. If there were a 3.5 rating overall that is what I would more accurately rate it, but this review is focused on my results of active daily wear for one year and what can most likely be expected in future use.I bought the Invicta 8926OB mainly for the following five reasons in order of importance:  1. 200m water resistance ensures it can be worn pretty much anywhere.  2. Automatic design negates the need for batteries.  3. All stainless steel silver color and construction looks clean and avoids the ugliness of gold colored plating scratching and wearing off.  4. Watch band is durable with large thick metal links.  5. Rolex Pro Diver look is classic and stylish. The back window displaying the internal parts is cool.However, I think I made the mistake of going with this watch as a daily wear after wearing a Seiko Kinetic Sports 50 for about 15 years. The main disappointment I had with the Seiko was that the gold tone wore off and scratched resulting in it looking dilapidated. Who wants to wear a dilapidated looking watch? I will never by a gold plated watch again (nor any other plated color). Also, the Seiko watch links were fairly small and weak and would bend if the watch bumped on something. Other than that though, the Seiko kept perfect time and never got a scratch on its Sapphlex watch face or window.So, when I bought the Invicta Pro Diver I was solving the problems I had with the Seiko; the entire watch is stainless steel silver with no colored plating so there is no color to scratch or wear off and the band links are larger and thicker, resisting damage. Yet, what I discovered was that there were other problems with the Invicta that the Seiko did not have. After one year of constant wear, here are the problems with this Invicta watch in order of importance to me;  1.  Watch window is only made of mineral and sticks out above the watch face. Within a month this watch began to get scratches on the window whereas the Seiko Sapphlex window did not get a single scratch in 15 years. This specific Invicta watch got a large deep scratch across the date magnifier and several smaller scratches near the edge of the window. Since the window is the highest part of the face of the watch and the magnifier sticks up even higher, both of them are prone to scratches. The scratch resistance of the watch could probably be improved by having the window inset deeper in the face. Previously I didn't realize the significance of the difference in window materials in watches, however, now I will never buy another watch with a mineral window again - it simply scratches too easily. I would rather pay more and a have a stronger longer lasting window.  2. Large crown knob unscrews too easily when it is hit or rubbed against something, potentially exposing the watch internals to water damage if not careful. The watch is not very water resistant with the knob unscrewed. This issue is a result of the combination of the large watch knob and the smaller guards, resulting in the knob sticking out too far. This issue could be resolved with a smaller knob, larger guards, or a combination of both.  3. Overall quality is somewhat low, but may not be out-of-line with the price:  a. Date magnifier on watch is not centered on the date - it's slight off counter-clockwise.  b. Rotating bezel markings do not align exactly with the time markings on the dial - they're not off by much, but it is noticeable.  c. Fluorescent illumination is very poor, only working well for a short time after the watch has been directly exposed to light.  d. Rotating bezel was very hard to rotate at first and then quit rotating clockwise, it can only be turned counter-clockwise now.  e. Watch movement gains an average of about 11 seconds per month. Apparently this is an excellent movement for this watch model, as other reviewers have reported much worse.  f. The Invicta one year warranty requires a $20 "handling" fee. If you do decide to buy this watch make sure to buy it with a good credit card that offers an extended warranty.In conclusion, while the price of this watch is fairly low and the design is really nice, if you're looking for a decent watch that you can wear daily and that will last I recommend going with something more expensive and of higher quality, particularly watches with either a sapphire or synthetic sapphire window. The window of the watch is probably one of the most important considerations for long term durability. This watch would probably be fine for limited and formal wear as more of a fashion accessory, but it simply does not stand up well to daily wear, especially if you have an active lifestyle.I am considering the more expensive Invicta 9937, which looks nearly identical, but at almost $300 there are other watches in that price range that appear to offer more for the money, like perpetual calendars and actual sapphire crystals rather than synthetic Flame Fusion. I'm also considering another Seiko watch since the last one I had was of high quality. I'm open to suggestions, but regardless of the brand of my next watch, I've learned that for daily wear the watch should be all stainless steel or solid silver colored metal and the window should be synthetic sapphire or better.11/14/14 Update: I read an interesting review from bmrider71 where he writes about replacing the mineral crystal with sapphire. He says the sapphire crystal only costs $30 retail. With the sapphire crystal being so cheap, Invicta should seriously consider offering a sapphire version of this watch for $30 more and maybe even dropping the mineral crystal altogether. That would result in a much more durable watch for only a little bit more money and would probably also result in a better reputation. If you would like to learn how to replace the crystal see the comment section of bmrider71's review here: http://www.amazon.com/review/R2NIG6B0SNNB8M/

January 2020 Update:Unfortunately I have had to downgrade this watch to 3 stars.  It now loses nearly a minute a day and as of last week it no longer winds itself. I wear it daily as I always have but now if I wind it up all the way, whether I just leave it on the bookshelf or wear it, it winds down in 43 hours (if not worn), to 44 hours (if being worn 17 hours a day).  Admittedly, 40+ hours is a good power reserve but I didn't buy this watch with the intention of having to manually wind it every day.  And by unscrewing and rescrewing the crown in every day it is only a matter of time before the delicate threads in the crown wear out.  If you buy this watch, plan to replace it every couple of years.  To me, that's too often.Original Review from 2017:I've had this watch for slightly over two weeks now and I am completely satisfied with it.  It arrived in perfect condition, and has not stopped running once since I originally set and wound it at 12:00am the morning of Sunday September 8th, even though I have left it off my wrist for as much as 16 hours at a time (usually around 8 hours each night).  Furthermore, for a mechanical (automatic) watch, it is keeping GREAT time.  It lost less than two minutes during the first two weeks of running (only about 7.5 seconds per day).I had originally planned on buying this less expensive Japanese Movement Invicta model only for wear when I have to be in the shadier parts of town (I am a musician), and I was going to buy the more expensive version, the Invicta 9937 with the Swiss Movement as my main watch.  But now, I fail to see a reason to spend the money on the "better" Invicta, given that this one is completely satisfactory to me so far at a cost that is more than two thirds less.If I have any longevity issues in the future I will be sure to update this review.  In the meantime, if you don't see any updates from me to the contrary, you can assume that this watch has been ticking along flawlessly since September 8, 2013.Note that I am a former (25+ years) Rolex owner, and I still would be if I hadn't made the mistake of leaving my Rolex out on my desk in my home office the day a Comcast Cable Repairman came to repair my faulty cable system - either he stole it, or my Rolex grew legs and walked out the door within minutes of him.October 16, 2013 UPDATE:Watch still looks great and runs great - no complaints.  It is losing a bit more time per day now - averaging a loss of 13.1 seconds per day during this past week.  This is still well within the realm of accuracy for Mechanical/Automatic Watches, and fantastic accuracy for an Automatic Watch that didn't even cost $100.  I'm sure my watch repairman could fine tune it and get it to be as accurate as my Rolex was - but it's not worth it to me when it is already this accurate.February 6, 2014 UPDATE:The watch is now losing about 25 seconds per day.  Eventually I'll get around to dropping it off at my watch repairman's place for an adjustment.  I still rate this watch at 5 stars.  I've had no problem with moisture getting inside, though it does get wet from time to time (not submerged), and the crystal and case are still scratch free though I do bump it into things from time to time (no, not on purpose).  Another plus:  On occasion I've left it on my nightstand for a day, and it's still running the next day.  And I often don't put it on until late afternoon or even early evening (I work and study at home) and again, it's never stopped.June 1, 2015 UPDATE:Slowly, we slow done...  The watch now loses about 40 seconds a day.  I've checked online and found many success stories and a few YouTube videos showing amateurs successfully regulating these watches, so I'll probably buy a tool to remove the watch's back and attempt to regulate it myself.  Heck, even if I ruined it, the cost of having a professional regulate the watch could be close to the cost of just buying another one.  And the very reputable watch repairman I called (5 Stars on Yelp) said if I brought it in, he'd give me a free estimate, saying it "might need more than an adjustment".  That sounded a bit ominous...  Given that its rate of slowing down has been so steady, I think it just needs an adjustment.  If and when I attempt it, I'll post the results.AUGUST 5, 2015 UPDATE:As I wrote in the previous update, the watch was gradually slowing down and was losing about 40 seconds a day.  Not wanting to potentially spend nearly as much on a professional adjustment as I paid when I purchased the watch new, I bought an "Abbest(TM) Watch Adjustable Opener Back Case Press Closer Remover Repair Watchmaker Tool" on Amazon ( http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00UAHDF3M ), studied a few YouTube tutorials on timing watches and took the plunge and timed my own watch.  And:  GREAT SUCCESS!!!  It took several weeks of going back and forth, setting the watch to run faster (then it would gain 10 to 30 seconds a day), then the next day I'd try to move the little lever as little as possible in the other direction, only to have it lose time each day.  The tiniest movement of that adjustment lever results in a lot of change in the watch's timing!  Sometimes I'd just push on the lever with my specialized tool (a toothpick) without seeing any physical movement of the lever happening, and yet find that the next day, it was running faster or slower.  My goal was to get it to gain no more than 5 seconds per day (and not lose time at all).  It took me around 10 or 12 days to reach my goal.  Since adjusting it on July 25th, it has averaged a gain of 4 seconds per day (and it's been a pretty consistent 4 seconds per day with very little variability day to day).  My wife thinks I am a bit OCD about it (she'd always happen by during the few moments each day when I'd be checking the watch against one of our Atomic Radio Clocks - hey - she's the one who bought the Atomic Radio Clocks, so SHE'S the one with the OCD issue!)..  :-)

Invicta 8926OB Automatic Diver WatchThe 8926OB differs from the 8926 due to the Original Bevel (OB) design, which is also called a coin-edge. The current 8926OB uses a Seiko Instruments NH35A movement, however the 8926OB's NH35A does not have any markings indicating country of origin for the NH35A. The SII manual for the NH35A shows either Japan or Malaysia, but it is not shown on the NH35A in the 8926OB! The watch face says Japan Movement, but the rotor on the NH35A should show this as well.The band feels very cheap, just like an average run of the mill Casio. The hinges are crimped/stamped steel and not like the higher-end Seiko, Citizen, or almost all of the typical Fossil watches. The safety clasp is extremely tight mainly to prevent accidentally releasing the band clasp while diving, but it is cumbersome to use. The band links are also made inconsistently. Some of them are a tight fit against another link, while other links are so loose that the pins fall right through. The links also bend forwards and backwards, not like the Fossil links which are sturdier.The unidirectional bezel is tight at first, but it has solid clicks and lines up properly. The watch face in my opinion is a bit small. I could confuse it for a lady's watch when used on a man's wrist. The watch itself is also plastered with Invicta logos and designs, which I feel are rather tacky. The magnifying lens / cyclops on the watch glass looks really out of place, as if they glued on a plastic lens to the watch glass. The worst part was that I actually found dust prints and residue underneath the watch glass.As for accuracy, don't expect any from this watch and movement. Even though it was within spec, I was losing 3-5 seconds per day when fully wound and inside an automatic watch winder. I understand that this is the nature of an automatic mechanical watch, but I just wanted to convey this again in case anyone was curious about it.I have another Invicta and was not impressed with its quality either. I won't be considering Invicta in the future. If you're fine with a cheaply made mall watch manufactured by a company with a questionable quality control reputation, Invicta is the brand to look at. The internal components are extremely cheap and flimsy. I honestly would say that you should consider Fossil before Invicta. At least Fossil has much better overall build quality and reliability.Overall: 3/5 stars, feels very cheaply made with a cheap feeling wrist band - reminds me of department store Casio wrist bands.

This being my first venture into automatic watches after doing quite a bit of looking at various options. I opted to go with the 8926 (mineral crystal,stamped clasp,miyota movement) over its more expensive cousin 9937 (flame fusion aka hybrid sapphire/mineral, solid clasp, swedish movement). Nevertheless, when I first got the watch--I was very impressed with the quality and appearance of the watch. The other reviewers who compared it to the Rolex Submariner aren't joking. It's very attractive watch. And it mirrors the appearance of the Submariner almost completely down to the coin edge except a couple of details: the luminescent dot for on the bezel is much larger on the Rolex, and the cyclops magnification on the 8926 is a joke. That being said, amazing bang for the buck. So I shook it around a bit to get it started and proceeded to wear it daily.A week in, I wake up to realize that it had stopped about an hour before I had woken up. Ok, charged it again. It died later on in the day. Now, when I try to charge it, it lasts maybe 3 minutes--I've tried both rocking it and winding it (40 turns is supposed to be enough for a full charge) but no avail. If you've done a bit research into Invicta timepieces, one thing you'll find is that many people complain about the quality control of their watches--and this I knew when I decided to purchase the watch. Oh well. Luckily it failed within the first 30 days so it's still covered by amazon. Time to get an exchange. Will update when I get the 2nd watch.UPDATE: So having received the replacement watch (Amazon customer support is great about sending out a replacement as soon as you file the claim so two thumbs up for them). I've had the watch for over a month now and it's working fine-unlike the first sample. Runs a couple minutes fast every month but that's to be expected for a sub-$100 automatic watch. So for the price, I'm quite happy with my purchase.WRAP-UP: Great watch in it's own right despite being a Submariner look-alike. I would recommend the watch if you are willing to take a chance with getting a really crappy watch that dies on you after amazon's return policy expires and you have to pay for shipping to send it to Invicta. So, the conclusion is that as the old adage 'you get what you pay for' still applies to this product, and though it is a handsome watch-you're taking your chances by buying one. Just pray you get lucky.

This is my second purchase of an Invicta pro diver. They occasionally drop below 70 bucks and at that price, it's hard to beat. I dislike most Invicta watches because they tend to be big and gross. This one is an attractive watch under 40mm. It owes its looks to the Rolex submariner its emulating. I've heard people complain about all the Invicta branding slathered all over this watch, but for an nh35 Seiko caliber automatic with 200 meters water resistant case....you can forgive a lot. If you want an automatic watch you won't mind being rough with, this is a nice option. Quality Control however can be kind of meh. The one I bought my son a few months back, the blue of the dial was almost purple compared to the bezel, once you notice it, you can't unsee it, and could drive you nuts.  this newest one I bought in black...and the bezel is very difficult to rotate compared to my son's. So I think cutting on quality control is one way they manage to sell these so darn cheap. Should not be a huge problem for me as I never planned to dive with this watch or even use the rotating bezel. I got a much better tool watches for that kind of work. This one makes a much better weekender than a workhorse. Put it on to knock out the honey-do list and if it takes a few bumps and bruises no big whoop.  My son plays contact sports wearing his and even the cheap hollow end link bracelet on his has endured well without breaking, Crystal holing up well too. All-around good deal, if you want, a cheap beater but not a fan of quartz. Of course, there is a quartz version available for even less! But for only about $15 difference in cost you might as well get the one with the Seiko automatic movement ... it's a very popular tried and true entry-level movement with hacking and hand winding. Chances are if you have other watches with hacking and hand winding that you paid between $100-$200 its probably a Seiko NH35. They work well, are easy to use and maintain, and tend to perform better than their specs might suggest

I have to say, I was a bit hesitant after reading so many negative reviews. They mostly focused on quality control issues, so not exactly faults of the watch in general, but issues with particular units. After receiving mine and testing it for a bit, I can say mine is not the worst, but it isn't' great either. About the movement, I have another watch with a similar one (NH36 vs this one's 35, only difference is the lack of day of the week) and it runs much better. The Invicta runs about +10-15 seconds a day, while the other one only runs about +5, and only lasts  a day after putting it down while the other one easily endures a couple of days. This is a bummer because with this Invicta I have to wear it every day, and not every other day like it was supposed to according to the movement's specs.Given this, I haven't tested the water resistance yet, lest I ruin the watch. I'll have my watchmaker check the o-rings first, in case they're old, dry or otherwise ruined.Overall it was still a good buy for the 70+€ I paid (with shipping). It's a beautiful watch, and probably the best sub homage in this price range, but by mass producing it in this scale they let a lot of bad apples slip by.

Many watch companies have made what may be regarded as homages to the Rolex Submariner. Invicta’s entry has much in its favor, especially for the price.The watch is powered by Seiko’s automatic NH35a movement, which is found on some watches costing hundreds more. The movement offers the options of stem winding and hacking (stopping the second hand for precise time setting), features not on the movement that Seiko itself typically uses for its Seiko 5 line of automatic watches.The case and dial are precisely and tastefully done, with water resistance aided by a screw-down crown. Especially nice touches are the observation back and the delicate Invicta logo that is shaped as a counter balance to the second hand. Invicta has received some criticism for putting its name on the side of the case. It is very precisely engraved and does not bother me at all.The bracelet has solid links except for the end links. However, they perfectly flow into the brushed and polished portions of the rest of the bracelet. My only wish list item for the bracelet would be a side button clasp release. However, the friction fit clasp does a secure job.My one major annoyance with this watch has to do with the rotating bezel. I initially received a watch with such a nearly impossibly tight bezel that I returned it for a replacement. The bezel on the replacement watch is much tighter than I would like, but usable. The bezel issue is the only reason I downgraded this review to four stars.

Received mine yesterday. It's a great Submariner homage for the cost. Looks are pretty dead-on, with the exception of the Invicta branding, which is, of course, what makes it an homage rather than an outright fake/copy. It's hard to beat 316L stainless steel, good looks, 200m water resistance, and a Seiko NH35 (which is hacking and hand-winding) at less than $100 US.For the record, the Invicta branding on the side of the case (which is what a LOT of people have an issue with) is very shallow and barely noticeable on mine. You wouldn't even notice it on a casual glance. I'd imagine that it could be ground/filed off very easily if it bothered you that much. The movement came in at +3 sec/day and 0.2ms beat error on my equipment, which is very good direct from the factory. The lume and the bracelet are the weak points here, but they aren't terrible. They're just not as strong as they could be, but at this price point they're both more than acceptable. It's eminently moddable, with I think the biggest two being possibly the bracelet and replacing the mineral crystal with sapphire, but you have to ask yourself if it's worth it to do such mods when they'll possibly cost more than the watch itself did.So, 4 out of 5. Strictly based on value, it's a 5/5, but I can't give it 5 stars due to the few slight weaknesses.

Great watch if you get the mechanical automatic version.  It uses a Seiko automatic movement. NOTE 1: This watch has a screw-down crown.  You must unscrew it to set the time & date.  You MUST remember to screw it back in before wearing it, or water can get inside. This watch offers a pretty substantial value for money. The 40mm size makes it much more wearable than some of the other massive offerings from invicta. The classic submariner style is also well done, but there’s no mistaking the watch for a Rolex. The applied invicta logos on the dial, counter balance on the seconds hand, clasp and side of the case may be a bit much, but they don’t bother me. With a claimed water resistance of 200m with the crown screwed in, I haven’t had any issues showering or doing dishes, and am not concerned about swimming with it. Mine in particular has also kept fairly outstanding time with the Seiko automatic NH35A running maybe just a few seconds a day fast (maybe +5 or so). In short, this watch stacks up extremely favorably in the inexpensive automatic sports watch category. If you’re considering a first auto, or just a beater sports watch for summer, this really works. Compare it to the seiko 5 sports line, or the orient ray/mako/Kanno/Kamasu models. They’re more expensive but some offer nicer features. Purchase one of these during a Prime sale for around $50-60 and you’re getting a heck of a deal! Objectively, this is a good, solid watch.

Shock cord In two of the three poles broke -- before I could put it up the second time! Before we went camping, I set it up, which was easy. I aired it out and used Coleman seam sealer as suggested in several reviews. Giving it time to dry, I took it down the next morning.Friday on Labor Day weekend, I went to put it up, and the shock cord simply unraveled on one pole -- broke. Undaunted I was going to figure out something. As I began to straighten the other long pole, same thing happened in the same way. At this point I was rather daunted.Fortunately, we were not camping far from home. I have two older tents in the garage -- much older. I was able to find two poles of about the same length and diameter. I was able to put up this new tent that way. It's not quite perfect, but it saved the weekend. To recap, I used poles from a tent that was over 10 years old, and the shock cord was still elastic enough and in good enough condition. Only the second time I tried to put of the new tent, the shock cord failed.It rained twice that weekend. Once it rained two hours straight without let up. The next time it rained off and on for several hours. There were no leaks at all. I cannot say if it would have without the seam sealer. One note, a good wind will blow in rain underneath the rain fly. The mesh makes up nearly all of two of the walls, and the rain fly only extends a few inches below. I suppose adjusting the guy lines or stakes might help keep out rain in a strong wind, but I can assure you the wind will blow in rain if it hits hard enough and from a certain direction. Beware.This is definitely not a cold weather tent -- not even a mid to late fall tent. Further, with the rain fly on and tightly secured, there is not that much air flow, and it did get it pretty warm (hot) inside. Adjusting the rain fly without completely removing it is possible and not too much of a headache.In conclusion, my experience with this tent leaves me giving it a one star, because that's all I can do. In fact, it's a negative five stars because it was broken and thus didn't work. Rarely throwing anything out saved me this time. It's past the return window, so I'm not entirely sure where to go from here. I suppose I can get two new poles somehow, but I'm not excited about paying to return the broken ones, which I assume they would want, as that will probably cost me around $15 dollars. Assuming the poles did work, the tent would have been fine. I'm not sure it was what we really needed, but that is on me for not better researching I suppose.

I was suffering from really annoying wrist pain, so I bought this wrist support.  The pain didn't go away, so I went to see an orthopedics doctor specializing in treating hand/wrist problems.  I showed him this strap, and here's some info I can provide which I hope will help:(1) I had tendinitis, with pain deep in the middle of the wrist, but also on the ulnar and radius sides, slightly upward on the forearm.(2) This wrist strap should have limited my wrist motion, but it doesn't have enough coverage (see comment below).  The tighter I strapped it on, the more my wrist remained fixed, but there was added pain from the compression of the strap, which also dug into the muscle between my thumb and first finger.  The limitation to wrist movement decreased when I eased off on the strap tension but that killed the support.(3) My doctor said there are two deficiencies here.  First, the sleeve needs to extend much farther up my forearm to provide support.  Second, there needs to be a stiff insert, commonly rigid plastic or metal (e.g., like the wrist protectors used by skateboarders), contained within the sleeve to ensure that my wrist will not move and stay "calm."Conclusion: I would not recommend this product to anyone who needs truly rigid support to calm a painful wrist.  If what is desired is a mildly-limiting device with minimal support, then this might work, but look for a heftier solution if you need a supplement to orthopedic treatment.

I am reminded today, upon erecting this tent for the first time, why it is such a gamble to shop for bulky (expensive-to-return) items online. The photo for this Coleman tent is very misleading. You think you are buying a four-sided tent with two windows, a door and a rainfly when, instead, with the rainfly removed it becomes apparent that it is a two wall tent with two of the four sides comprised only of mesh. While this may be ideal for summer ventilation, it's not good for privacy as there is a gap between the rainfly and the bottom edge of the "windows". Without that rainfly in place, there is no remaining privacy in the tent to speak of thanks to the "open sided" design.My goal was to purchase a tent that could work in emergency situations, such as the aftermath of an earthquake, where people do not feel safe (or their home isn't safe) to reenter. (Alas, I was reminded, after the recent 7.1 and 6.4 July 4 holiday weekend earthquakes here in California, that access to a quick form of shelter is a big part of emergency preparedness.)Where I live, rain is rarely the issue as much as wind. This tent design is likely to take on a lot of blowing dust because two out of the four sides can't be zipped up — Coleman has given no option to close either "window". (A drop-down window shade would have been nice even if the only means of securing them was an option to tie them to the sidewalls!). Meanwhile, because the rainfly is a bit too small, wind (and possibly rain) can enter the tent even when it the rainfly is in place. What's more, the presence of the two largely opened sides means that the tent will feel drafty in cooler weather. (For summer camping this may not be a deal breaker but for emergency use — when you can't pick your weather or your season — it could be a *big* problem.)I spent hours shopping for a tent yet was unprepared for what I would receive despite comparing reviews on numerous tents in the four-to-six person size range. In hindsight, I can only speculate that this tent is well reviewed because many reviewers live areas where summer storms are more common than they are here in California — in which case keeping the rainfly on with each and every use is to be expected. Ideally, however, use of the rainfly would have been optional and tent privacy would not have been the worse for having left it off. (A related drawback to this design is that if the rainfly is damaged, the tent will provide no real protection from the elements because there is no way to close the windows from the interior of the tent.) What's more, in the course of my research, I learned that Coleman doesn't offer much in the way of replaceable parts for tents under ~$300 so if the rainfly rips or a pole breaks, it's essentially scrap heap time.If you intend to use this tent only for summer camping and don't mind gaps between the rainfly and the "windows" because you camp predominately in isolated (private/secluded) areas, this tent might be for you. However, if you want the option to close up the mesh "windows" (sides) to improve privacy or cut down dust and drafts — or you're simply concerned that wind-blown rain may enter the tent from beneath the rainfly — then my suggestion to you is to keep on looking.

The key ( pardon the pun)  is to never leave your bike in the dark.  Never leave your bike for extended periods with just a lock to protect it.  A bike lock will protect your bike for a short period (3-4 hours)  up to a full day at work in the daylight .  All bets are off at night .  Treat your bike as you would your two-year-old child .  Sure, you could lock him/her to a street sign for a short period of time with good expectations of finding him/her upon your return. You leave that kid out overnight, no baby tomorrow.  In my world a bike lock provides a degree of protection when a  thief  is in full view of the public.  A bike lock is meant to slow down the process of stealing your bike.  I have never /  will never own a gun.  However I would enjoy seeing the rotting carcass of a bike thief lying in a pool of his blood next to the last bike he tried to steal. I've used this twice now and I have some mixed feelings on this luxury item...The Good!My idea of outdoor adventures is to find an area, setup camp, use a couple days to explore/decompress, and of course be 'one' with nature.  On our second to last trip we had eight people with us and this item was perfect for illuminating a ~6000 square foot area.  I won't complain about how bright these are, they're pretty powerful in that regard.The Maybe...Most of my camping is going to be backpacking and sometimes it's nice to spice up the trip a few luxury items.  I think these lanterns would qualify as a luxury item.  If you're sharing the load for an adventure into the wilderness? Sure. These might make things a little easier at camp but I don't think I would take this on a solo or high-mileage trip.  They're just too heavy and (one of these) take up too much space in your pack.  However, that's for you to decide.  Some people don't mind the extra space.  Personally, I like to keep my base weights between 10 to 15 pounds.  The lantern weights just over 10 ounces with batteries, that's too much for it's  functional use.So, who is this for?In my opinion? Everyone.  It's good for emergency use and great for car and campground camping.  I think it's an acceptable luxury item for backpacking, especially if your splitting the load between a couple or few people.  I just wouldn't take this on any solo trip or high mileage trip.How about it's design flaws and quality?I wish the hanging handles would snap to the sides.  Additionally,  I would also venture to say these lanterns are not very waterproof.  When deployed open, these lanterns expose areas where water can get inside the enclosure.  They're probably going to get damaged in any type of fall greater than a meter... These don't feel that solid and I am not expecting years on these lanterns...  Come on, these things are without a doubt cheaply made.  I think that's reflected in the price, just remember what you're buying.Final thoughts...For emergency use and those few times per year campers? This is not a horrible product... I think it'll work well for you and it keeps those activities affordable.  Backpacking? You be the judge.Thanks for reading.

The purchase of this tent was predicated on reviews I read online. Most important to me was its waterproofing feature which I found not to be so great. It rained during the early morning , not heavily but a constant  drizzle for sometime. In the morning I opened the tent to find water in every corner on the inside. It was most in the corner where there is a small zipper to allow passage of an extension cord. I had passed through an extension cord a zippered up the best I can. I investigated and found that about 6-8 inches of seam away from each corner had pin holes associated with the stitching. Had I stretched those areas too much when I installed the pegs? Who knows. In any case I acquired a tube of a tent sealant and ran it generously in those areas that seemed compromised. I will follow up with a test after a few days . Other than that I am pleased with this tent so far.Update: So I applied a product , tent seal , which is a liquid , along the seams  of the problem areas , the corners. I applied inside as well as outside about 15 inches or so away from each corner. It drizzled again for an hour or so and all corners except the corner with the through hole for an extension cord was dry. This time though I did not have an extension cord passing through and the zipper was closed all the way. Well this area (corner) had a puddle of water on the floor. There was water in the seam where the upper fabric meets the lower tarp part, so water had to be coming in from that location . I also found the entire zipper to be wet even though the outer flap had covered it.I will wait for that area to dry out and then retreat with  the tent sealant. I will report back.UPDATE Number 2. So I applied tent sealant in the zip area where one can pass through an extension cord. It rained heavily last night and when I checked for water on the inside there only a few drops. So that is much better. The Zipper still got wet so I am thinking of adding somehow a layer of waterproof fabric in that area to reduce or eliminate the entrance of water. Having said that I see in the product description that this tent is now water resistance as opposed to waterproof.

I purchased this tent largely based on the number of reviews, which at the time was 4.5 stars, the size, and that it had a rain fly. It was pretty easy to setup alone, but needs two people to raise the tent once the poles are inserted. This review is after one week end of camping in Colorado at 8000 ft, 85 degrees during the day, and 48 degrees at night. I’ll update after the next.Pros:1. Hook inside on top, to hang a lightweight LED light.2. Side pockets to store smaller items.3. Pretty easy to setup.4. Price was good at almost $100Cons:1. Two sides have large non-zipping screens, air can freely flow through the tent. The first night we used it we were extremely cold, our feet and head were freezing in the middle of the night. I expected a bit more insulation, and our sleeping bags were not rated for really cold weather. I didn’t realize there was no way to seal up the sides for cold nights, a HUGE flaw in my opinion. The rain fly sits away from the tent when staked, so you can’t trap any warm air inside. Our 2nd and 3rd night camping, I removed the rain fly stakes to let the fly rest loosely against the mesh sides, and this helped a bit - however, had is been rainy or windy we’d have had a different problem.2. My wife was hooking one of the tent side hooks to the poles, and the base of it partially ripped away from the tent. I imagine those hooks will wear out rather quickly considering how easily the sewing ripped.3. It seems like small rocks on the ground have almost penetrated the flooring near the entrance. We alway take our shoes off before entering, so I thought this was odd. I’m curious how this will hold up over time, and if we’ll get holes.4. After handling the fiberglass poles, I got fiberglass splinters in 2 fingers. I’ve started only grabbing the metal parts when I can. This may be totally normal, but just reporting my findings here.5. We bought the 6 person version, and I can’t imagine 6 people sleeping in this tent. I could probably sleep 20+ babies in there, but let’s be real. We slept 4 wide, with some smaller bags at our feet, and that filled the tent. I’d layout your sleeping bags and see what’s realistic for how many you could fit inside.Overall I’d say this tent is ok. I had thought buying a tent with the Coleman name on it would be a safe bet, but I’m not very impressed with this one. With that being said, it was $100, so you get what you pay for.Update Aug 23, 2020:We took this tent to a lake on the plains. Day temp 98, low of 60. We were much more comfortable this time, of course it was pretty hot, and it didn't cool off quickly at night. The tent was just what we needed for this hot weather, and our second time using this tent was even quicker to setup. If only the sides zipped up, that might help with cooler temperatures. No complaints this trip.

For camping out of a vehicle, the tent packs up nicely.  The set up, with one person, is very easy.  This tent is also roomy.  Additionally, the floor to this tent comes up a few inches off the ground before joining to the walls.  This helps to ensure the seams are above the ground, preventing water from coming through the seams.  That is about where the the good points stop.I set this tent up, alone, in about 15mph winds while out on a hunting trip.  I managed to set the tent up solo, so no complaints.  Now, keep in mind, I am in Southern Arizona with ground harder than concrete.  After set up, I properly staked the tent, and set up the rain fly.  During the night, the winds kicked up in excess of 20mph. At first, one corner came unstaked due to the wind.  This tent is like a parachute in the wind, by the way.  I restaked the corner at about midnight.  A little later, another corner came unstaked, again due to the high winds.  Again, I restaked the corner.  Wouldn't you know it? Less than an hour later, both corners (the front corners) came unstaked and the front of the tent lifted up due to the high winds and enormous size of this tent.  I found myself (6'3", 240lbs) inside this tent trying to keep it from blowing away with the door completely above my head; It was a disaster of a night to say the least.  I ended up throwing this tent in my Jeep and sleeping in the Jeep for the night.  For the rest of the hunt, I slept in my two person North Face tent, which is made to handle high winds and adverse weather.Now, if you are camping from a vehicle in good weather, this is your tent. If the winds pick up, you're in for a bad night.  This tent is too big and not secure enough to be in windy weather.  I will say that I have not been in this tent in the rain.  However, I am still bringing this tent on my next hunt in a few weeks.  I will be in Northern Arizona surrounded by trees, which help to block wind. Nevertheless, based on my last experience, I am bringing my North Face Tent in the even this tent does not hold up to the weather up north.  I will update this review if needed.The reason I went with this tent, even though I own a great two person North Face, is the size.  When I am out hunting for a week at a time and I have my vehicle near by, I like to bring an air-mattress and have room to actually stand up and move around.  Having a central place to camp is great for big tents like this Coleman. If you can set up a tent in one spot for a few days, a big tent is a welcoming comfort.

Backstory: I bought this wrist brace for work. I do assembly work and often have to use power tools to assemble things at odd angles that are not conducive to a healthy wrist. This helps to reduce the symptoms of carpal tunnel syndrome.Pros:+ Provides adequate support and range of motion while working at 9-12 hour days.+ Machine washable in cold gentle cycle! Very important if using it as a daily work use.+ Small enough to carry in a pocket for when you need to take it off to give your wrist some air+ Comes with an informational packet with wrist exercises to help rehabilitate your carpal tunnel.Cons:- Inner thumb loop is not sewn with a comfortable fabric cover. This is not conducive to use over a long period as you will feel the friction of the rough edge of the fabric brush against your thumb webbing throughout the day. This can lead to irritation, discomfort, and soreness due to the abrasion from the uncovered material.- To some, the one-size-fits-all model might be a con. If you have small wrists, this can lead to a bulky gathering of material on your wrist. This makes it hard to wear gloves over it if you work with tools all day.Conclusion: The wrist brace is not the most comfortable, especially if you work in manual labor. I do not imagine the comfort issue being major if you work in a white collar environment. This is great if you simply need a bit of wrist support and do not want the stiffness of a brace with a splint. The biggest value, in my opinion, is the informational packet to help you rehabilitate and strengthen your wrist and forearm to combat and prevent carpal tunnel syndrome. Would I recommend the brace itself? Yes, if you are looking for a flexible support. No if you are working in manual labor and will require the constant use of your hands to grip items as this seems to be the source of the discomfort. If the thumb ring had a fabric covering similar to the rest of the outline of the product, I imagine this would not be an issue. As for the durability, I cannot speak to it in the long-term sense as I have only owned this product for one week. However, I have used it as my daily-use flexible brace for work and tested it for 45 hours this past week and found it to be relatively satisfactory at relieving carpal tunnel syndrome to reduce pain and tingling in my hand.

The tent was super easy to put up and take down, the only issue was the stakes that were provided. They were pretty wimpy, so I would recommend buying separate ones if you know it’s gonna be windy and your hammering them into harder ground.
Camping was planned ahead of time. But after the tent was setup, I realized that it was a military colour. Maybe it should have been orange. At that moment, I preferred to go back home.
Easy to set up and take down. Not sure if you could fit in 4 full grown people in this bad boy, it would be a very tight squeeze. Perfect for me and the boy, probably fit 3 comfortably

The Coleman tent is very easy to set up. Roomy for two people.The only issue I had with the tent is that, it appears that the bottom, the all Grey section, has a hint of fiberglass in the material.  I couldn't tell you how many charred pieces I pulled out of my hands. I highly recommend wearing protective gloves when handling this product. I know I will.

I owned the older version of this tent for almost 20 yrs and it held up great. I'm not sure if the new model is bigger than the old, but I thought I owned the 4 person tent in the past. If you always plan to camp with another person(s), this new 4 person tent is great. You can have enough room for two and even put camp chairs in it and use it as a screened room since the side windows are so big. However, if you plan to camp by yourself sometimes, I would get the 3 person tent. The 4 person is difficult to put up on with one person and I would not want to have to do it on my own while it's raining. Something else I liked with the old model is the full screen front door. The new models only have a half screen front door. No more laying in the sleeping bag and gazing out the door into the woods. But the huge side screens do allow for better star gazing.
Easy set up great quality - 4 star because the carry bag is SO SMALL to get it folded back up and able to fit is like a magic trick otherwise would have been a 5 star

First of all, it says it's for 4 person but it's for 2 person I can say. Maybe 2 person plus 1 child. But not for 4 adults.We used the 4 person Coleman Sundome tent for camping in Virginia. It was easy to assemble the tent even for one person. It took like 15-20 mins to build up. Everything was okay except the weatherproof feature. It was not that cold outside but we felt cold. Even with this disadvantage, Coleman deserves  at least 4 star because of the other products I've been using like sleep bag etc.

Although it is water resistant and waterproof lightweight it is not. Glorified camping it is no problem, you pull it out your vehicle and set it up. One person could do it,but two is preferable. To carry this on a trek for two or three day's im not sure would be ideal. Carrying case for this is not designed for trekking.

I have not had a chance to test this tent out during rain yet, but so far, it held up really well to strong blustery winds and kept the dust out. Very easy to setup even by oneself and easy to wash and put away.

My son wanted his own tent. He never camped before, being 12, I let him in the backyard over the weekend. Of course, it rained and he was soaked. I'll just have to buy some waterproofing spray 🤷🏽‍♀️ but he was excited on how easy it was to put up.
Its better than the shelter half i had in SE Asia!!

Used it for the first time last weekend in 55 degree night weather for my daughter & her bestie. They bundled up & were fine all night even though the windows don't zip up. Still wish there was a way for that, but it's a decent summer tent.Easy to set up. My 12 year old son did it with no issues.

Easy to set up. Roomy but for only two or three. Four would have no extra room for stuff. Somewhat lightweight. Was hoping for a little more durable looking. Have not had long, but previous model started leaking after a couple years. Have not had this one rain tested yet, but it does have a bottom protection that comes up the sides farther which seems like it might keep deeper rain out. Good rain shield over top. Good window placement for circulation.

I’m no tent expert what so ever. This is the first tent I’ve ever bought & it was for my first time camping as an adult.SET UP:I didn’t practice setting up before going camping like I should’ve, & arrived at the camp site in the dark. So I set up the tent in the dark, by myself, with only a lantern & a flashlight. That being said I’d still say it was a easy set up. Took about 20 minutes due to everything I stated above but had I practiced before I could see this being a easy 10 min set up. Maybe even less.WEATHERPROOF:I sprayed my tent with water repellent after set up. I went camping right by the beach so there was definitely moisture in the air. There was water droplets on the tent in the morning but I didn’t see any water in the tent. I did however feel like on of the ends of my blanket felt slightly damp but it could’ve just been really cold as it was up against the side of the tent all night. I think it would hold up in light rain or mild wind but definitely not for a storm or even heavy rain & winds.FOR THE NEW CAMPERS LIKE ME:I was expecting the 3person tent to fit 3 ppl and have room for bags but that isn’t the case. Apparently that’s not how tents work. A 3 person tent literally fits 3 ppl sleeping, no extra room.
You get what you paid for. It is good for it's price, just a little tiny for two people. If you want a bigger or better quality you gotta spend more money.
Just use it once. So far it is great. Good for 2 person.

Good at what it is, but you must understand what that really is first. Like most tents actually only fits 50% of stated people. Two could sleep in this if they are on the smaller side and don’t mind physically touching the whole time or leaving gear outside. Otherwise it’s only good for one person. It works well enough though. Light and small when packed up, but wouldn’t take it backpacking. Stands tall against wind and easy to set up. Stakes suck though, invest in better ones before your first trip. Haven’t tried it in rain, don’t plan to.

The tent went through a flash flood and I stayed dry :-) true to Coleman quality. That said I tried this style because I would not have to carry it backpacking. I like that I can stand up inside the tent. Something is going on with the floor dimensions and the height that I get floor creep; the tent sides creep up if I do not have holders on the corners inside. Yes, I use the stakes. The stakes move. I still consider it a good tent for what I use it for. Thx!

Exchanged it for a tent that I can stand up in, and one that I can put up by myself.  I am a 68 year old female with mildly arthritic hands and the buttons on the poles are mostly too difficult to push.

Great for one person, two would be too tight. I’m 5’9”. Plenty spacious.Pretty easy setup. I hate feeding poles thru casings, but this tent’s not too bad. I was in very mild weather on the CA coast. 45 degrees at night, almost no wind. Very compact and lightweight when it’s packed up. Easy to disassemble. Good choice for me.
A good, inexpensive tent that has plenty of room for four people and some equipment. Tents are always rated for more people than can comfortably fit.

It's nice, compact and light weight tent for it's size. It's waterproof and didn't got any issues while camping in rain. Very easy to setup. I'm give 4 instead of 5 star as entry place of tent is having very small shading to prevent rain to get in while using it during rain and also due to small shading can't leave footwear outside when it's raining.

Year #3 and the tent is still going strong. We use this for our two you g sons and it has held up to their rolling/romping inside it for several summers now. I think it’s great for kids, but a bit small for adults. We have to put our queen air mat inside it before we blow it up because it won’t fit through the door blown up. The air mat fills the whole floor and is tight against the  walls, which isn’t good if you get rained on, but if you have an additional canopy it’s not an issue. The tent did well in a rainstorm once... the only thing that got wet was the spot where the mattress touches the side. Overall we are happy with this tent.

Standard tent other than the assembly. You have to bend two of the sticks, when there is no clip or anything to keep the sticks in place while you’re bending one side. My suggestion if you are dealing with this test, is to stick one side into the ground, to act is that clip.
Love it.. the only issue is the cheap plastic clips and the weak stakes...

One thing I saw immediately: it's a really small 2-man. I only needed it for myself, and it was perfect for me. I was able to keep all my gear inside and had plenty of room to get in and out. If there were two people, it would have been really tight, and the second person's face would have been right up against the tent flap. My previous tent was a 4-man, and it accommodated two people and two dogs very comfortably with gear. Not much room for any additional people. I'm not sure who these tents get tested on, but they must be really short and really thin. I'm 5'3" and there wasn't a lot of spare room once I had my pillow at one end. I don't think I could have stretched out if I was more than 5'8." The rainfly was a bit of a struggle to get fastened. Other than that, I was able to pitch it pretty easily. It also actually did fit back in its bag, too, through 2 campsites.
Its a good tent
Not really waterproof. it rained a little bit & it leaked through
Acceptable value

I have very little to complain about this camping tent. However, the mounting pegs bend way too easy and should be reinforced for future product releases. Different camp sites require different mounting force. These pegs are not designed for tough earth that is for sure.Wouldn't buy again. Had to get different pegs after camping trip.
Very lightweight. Too bright for me, was super bright in the morning

The Coleman tent is a free-standing tent, a feature that makes it easier to install. You'll only need ten minutes to set-up your tent. It is dome-shaped and comes with fiberglass poles that are 8.5mm thick. These poles feature Insta-Clip attachments for easy installation and help the tent to stand up against any intensity of the wind. The pole sleeves are continuous and snag-free, a feature that makes it easy to install. The tent’s canopy is high-performing and durable polyester, while the floor features the sturdy 1000D Polyethylene. The tent is 33-percent more water resistant as compared to any other product from Coleman. Its ability to withstand strong gusts of wind is unmatched. The unique design allows for its unparalleled services. With a WeatherTec is a robust system that protects against weather elements. Overall, this is a durable, free-standing, spacious, cost-friendly tent.
5 years later, still holding strong. Expecting it to not last much longer. Money well sent.

Easy to assemble and well constructed to boot.  I would love to see the size of the four humans who were used in the sizing tests for Coleman though.  The tent is very open and not suitable for cold temperatures even with the fly installed.  My only minor complaint is that water enters the tent when you unzip the main opening because the flap basically falls inside the tent.  Maybe I’ll figure out a way to keep it from happening with more use.

So I bought this for a camping trip this summer up by the coast. It was fine during the day but at night the wind blew right in and cold seeped into this tent. I was sleeping with a lot of blankets, a big comforter, flannel sheets and another person on a tall air matress elevated from the ground and it was still freezing. Would only recommend for any place that doesn’t get below 60 at night. I didn’t realize when I bought the tent that the big “ mesh windows” were always windows. As in there is no zipper flap to cover the mesh with a more solid fabric so they are always open, which also means without the rain fly you would have no privacy. It didn’t really rain while we were camping but it did get moist on a few of the days and the rain fly did keep the water out. It does say in the description that it’s good for warm weather but also makes it sound like it can withstand some mildly cold weather by stating that it can withstand winds and rain and I feel like a paid a lot for a tent that is neither that big nor good for any weather that isn’t 70 or above.

A lovely little tent for casual car camping. Survived two days in pretty torrential rain with minimal seepage. This is a great starter tent. Big enough for 2 comfortably.  or 1 with room to spread out and store gear.
We just use this as a backyard tent for the grand-kids. I set it up and took it down by myself without any trouble. I cannot vouch for durability or how well it would hold up in rough weather.

I do love the tent. I only went 4 stars because one tent pole was broken on delivery, and even though the tent is "under warranty" Coleman warranty department did not respond to calls or emails. Fortunately with a bit of research I was able to fix it for $5.
Nice tent
A bit of a tight squeeze for two. Will fit a inflatable queen "wall to wall" however, it is a tight fit. I was comfortable, bf not so much 😂Served its purpose and worth the price.

Product is quality as is the case with all Coleman products.  Well designed and thoughtful touches.  Easy to erect.  Nice cross ventilation.  You will need to buy screw type stakes if you are beach camping which is to be expected.  Tent does flex in higher beach winds but maintains its structure.  Advertised as 4 person tent but realistically is a two adult tent with a full air mattress.  Light weight, can

Great lightweight tent, easy to set up and pack away. Didn’t get it wet yet but it seems nice. I would only use for two adults or four kids.

I didn't realize when I bought this tent (though I looked at the pictures) that the sides are mesh--with no covering.  There is a rain cover that covers the mesh, but it doesn't have anything like a zipper closure from the inside to cover the mesh.  I've only used it in warm weather and from what I can tell it would only be a warm weather tent.  It is very easy to put up and take down. I got the six person tent and it fits two single air mattresses with room at the end and between the beds.  Can also easily stand up inside.
Windy day in Colorado and the tent blew away. I would give it five stars but it wasn’t 100% weatherproof
The dimensions were unclear in the description as it lists multiple different measurements. Its a bit small but will work fine for a single person. Worth the price.

These are way smaller than advertised. I mean you could sit as many people in there. But sleeping would be another matter entirely.That being said my wife and I took this to a trip to Big Bend, and we had flooding and rain and no backup plan. The wind was so strong that the tent would fold over entirely during gusts that would last for 10 second. But it popped right back up every single time. And the inside of the tent was bone dry. Even though we had standing water outside, and flooding.It's dinky and small but it held up to weather I figured we'd be sleeping in the car for. I don't know how many trips like that it'll last on. But it did amazing well under that kind of stress.
It’s a great tent, but the zipper on the front door busted the first time we took it out.

Tent was smaller than I expected but fit a queen air mattress.  No extra room for activities, getting dressed was an Olympic sport.  We had to leave our suitcase in the car.  Tent was easy to set up and had all its parts.  We didn't experience any rain or wind.

I enjoyed the larger space than my last tent. I also appreciated the ease of setting up the tent. Unlike my last tent this style did not have an entrance over flap with roof and sides. Although even being a small space I could put wet shoes etc outside the tent and they would dry. It saved dirt, sand, debris outside the tent.
My fiancé have taken our new tent camping and have absolutely loved it! We stayed comfortable and had privacy.

Just bought this tent and took it out this weekend. Was warm and dry so I can’t speak on how it handles the rain or the cold, but it handled some VERY strong winds like a champ. The ventilation is great, and if you don’t need the rain fly it’s great to see the stars. It’s super easy to set up and take down and it packs pretty light! I would say it is a little tight for two people but still manageable. Overall a great tent, really glad I bought it!
Only used it onceeasy set up.Nice little tent
Excellent quality
Good tent. Easy set up, like really easy.  Fit 3 campers with room to spare. Haven’t had to test it in the rain yet. It’s heavy but for car camping it’s a great tent for the money.

I do not like at all that the windows do not have zippered covers over the screens, I would not have purchased this tent had I known this; screen windows only get covered with using rain guard.  The front door has screen zipper covering which is great.
Great size, not sure on water proof and weather yet. Folding it back in the bag is really hard.
Good tent. Fits a queen size air bed length-wise. Good air flow for warmer nights. Not great during cold nights.

This is a basic Coleman tent for occasional summer camping. It looks nice, but can take water if it rains long enough. This is without saying not a backpacker tent but is suitable for Cub Scout or car camping. The room and head space in the middle is decent and the floor space works as described if you are careful with what you bring in. The poles seem to break and the fabric tears over a few seasons, but if you are gentle and dry it out before putting it away it should be worth the money. If you are looking for something more lightweight or durable look for a higher price point brand as Coleman is for basic car camping use where you do not have to carry it far.
Very good for the price. Very satisfied with coleman product.had many over the years.
nice little tent

This tent is amazing but it is small. A grown man probably cannot fit in the tent comfortably but it is lightweight, easily constructed, and appealing to the eye. I recommend this tent to the shorter people who aren't claustrophobic!
Great product. Used it for weekend camping. Easy up and stow away. The weather was great so unable to comment on that.
I have used Coleman before. This product in good in almost all terms, except won't withstand wind probably because the rods are into semi tent and does not cover the whole area
Nice for weekend trip for a couple people. Plenty of walkaround room And nice to be able to stand up.

Tent worked perfectly and was very easy to set up. Only draw back is the stakes to hold it down are garbage. If the ground is at all hard, they will just bend and not go in. This makes it very hard to secure the tent.  Upgraded stakes and problem solved
Awesome for summer fun

to Coleman and every other tent/sleeping bag company -- Why do you make your bags so small!!! We do overnight and back yard camping and the worst part of every experience is trying to get the tent back into the bag. Our fun trips end in frustration as we sweat to get two people to jam the tent in and try to force the zipper up. This makes no sense! Just make the bags bigger! Excellent product

Good tent for the price.  It rained on us one night and water came in through a couple areas.  It's mostly as the rain was sideways and the rain fly doesn't go as low as needed to keep that kind of rain out.

I purchased this tent to pack on a Harley Davidson Heritage Classic with passenger seat and back rest. The carrying handles were long enough to slip over the back rest to secure it. The tent was quick to set up, provides great ventilation, did not collect condensation on a 30 degree F night, no gaps in door zipper(kept out all insects). As for size; I had a twin size air mattress which nearly covered the entire footprint of the tent. I had just enough room to stow my backpack, helmet, and leather goods. Tent stakes are very thin and bend very easily, I recommend purchasing heavier duty stakes before using this tent! Other than that it was a great tent for ONE person.
Easy to set up, room for queen and twin air mattress and gear. Came with small tear in mesh at the top center, not good but doesn't impact structure.
Tent is great, much larger and taller than expected. Four stars because the rope in the fly tent poles were cut so we have to get replacement poles for the fly.
Definitely worth the purchase, great brand. Rained the night we camped and no rain came in at all.

Seems to be "as advertised".Held up well in light rain. NOT something you want to try to put up in the dark. It is small but is an emergency shelter for my small generator.My only real complaint is that i paid $38.22 + tax. Kinda high i think.
Very nice tent. However its more of a 4 person then 6. Fits a queen and a full air mattress inside.
Not for backpacking by any means, a pretty heavy tent, but a nice one to use for car camping. taken it out a few times no issues with weather

We have the 6 man version tent before - which has been great for a lot of outings.  We needed a smaller one so we could have more family come with us in our Aframe trailer.  We ordered the three man version and it has worked very well so far.  It only lost one star since - I think the fabric around the zipper is easily caught in the teeth.  I got it stuck and unstuck twice.  Be careful / aware when using the product.

Was going on some weekend car camping trips with friends and family.  My 2 nephews needed a tent and i looked and found this for a decent price.  Almost chose the @ person tent.  But, I currently have another 2p tent and for me alone it is a little snug when I put my pack and gear in with me.  So, I selected the 3p version...best choice ever.  Set up was not complicated, infact my nephews put it up themselves  in just a few minutes.  My 2 nephews fit comfortably and they even had room for their packs and some gear.  Its by no means a minimalist tent but,  it only weighed 2-3 lb. packed.  In the interior, there is a loop at the center to hang a lamp.  It also has 2 storage pockets for gear.  Since it's the middle of summer, I cant say much about how weather proof it is.  But, it did well against the occasional  water spray.  It also came with a  small tarp to be used like a door mat.  One short fall was that it didn't come with a footprint tarp.  But, I  easily fixed that with a spare one I had in my gear bin.  Only used this tent a couple times this summer and it performed well on our weekend trips.  Overall, gave it four stars because of the price at the time and it performed well for what we needed.  Would purchase again if I need another.  Thanks

I was so anxious about how to set it up before I camped, but it took me less than 10 minutes to pitch it. However, if you camp in a cold place, you get cold because the air comes through it. I am taking off one star because of that reason.

Very nice tent for the price.The only complaint is that stakes included are too cheap. They are pretty much useless if used on the area with small gravels, bent easily.Other than that I can't complain for a $70 tent. Make sure to get a separate set of stakes.

We purchased this tent so that my husband could stand up and not have to crouch while in the tent. We used it on a week long trip and had no issues. It rained and everything stayed dry. We have not tested it in a thunder storm with heavy wind/rain but we are satisfied so far. I was concerned with some of the negative reviews about the sturdiness of the poles but we had no issues. We have multiple tents in varying sizes from r different activities and we were completely satisfied with this one.
Easy to put together. The onlyProblem I had was the condensation on the sides of the tent. That was a little much. The outside was dry, and no water came in through the top.

Overall, this is a safe bet for 2 people that don't mind getting cozy. If a heavy rain is in the forecast, bring an extra tarp. Or more towels.Pros:~ Setup is fairly easy and quick. If you've set up a tent before ever in your life, you'll understand how to set this one up.~ Great views at night if you choose to sleep without the rainfly, due to a generously sized screened roof.~ The addition of the small doormat-type tarp is thoughtful. Even more effective if you buy an inexpensive rug to go on top of that to remove sand and debris from your feet before entering.~ Relatively lightweight. Could serve as a hiking tent for overnight trips.Cons:~ Have a heavy duty ground tarp. I used this tent fresh out of the box with a ground tarp and still ended up with  damage to the floor~ We had steady rainfall for 12-18 hours, and water came in at all 4 corners where the nylon joins to the tub. Being brand new, I didn't think I would need to seal the seams. Apparently, I was wrong.~ Like most tents, this was hot and muggy with the rainfly on, so either be ok with that, or bring a fan.~ If you use this without a rainfly, be aware of who's around if you sleep in the nude or plan to change your clothes. You WILL give someone a show if you're not careful.~ Definitely only fits 2 adults who like each other. Or maybe 3 small, uncommonly cooperative children. It says it would fit a queen size air mattress- I don't know how. With a single cot and air mattress topper, I was out of space.~ Comes with the standard cheap wire stakes. Toss those and get something a little more substantial, like a heavy plastic stake or yard nails.

Easy set up and Light weight. Not much options to additional storage in side but very good quality and stood strong during high winds and stayed dry during a rain. This is a perfect tent for the casual camper but maybe worth  spending a little more  money for more heavy duty tent for longer and frequent  trips.

I bought this tent in the summer of 2020 to gain some distance from my parents who I still live with with my partner.  We are both in our late twenties and so its nice to have some space.  Its a good tent, though I don't see how it could even sleep four incredibly skinny adults.  Three very close friends would be a stretch, as it barely fits our Queen size air mattress.  However there's enough room at the bottom of the tent to stow my partner's bow, arrows quiver, our hiking bag and two backpacks.  The main downside is that there are no side pockets and the two overhead pockets are at either end of the tent.  I put a flashlight in one of the pockets and cracked my head against it three times in the night when I rolled over and forgot it was there.  It also gets hot during the day, but at night it gives a great view of the stars.  I live in California and its been in the 90's for the past several days, I have to get up at nine, otherwise its way too hot inside of the tent.  I have not yet put on the rainfly, nor has it been through the rain, truthfully we'd most likely pack it up before having be pelted with rain.  It blew over once, when we left for a few days and left only the mattress and sleeping bag inside it.  However I live in an area with high winds by the ocean and so that may have something to do with it blowing over.
not the best one but im satisfied
if you have 3 people, make sure buy tent for 6 people, this is too small for 3 people.
Easy to put together, but I was expecting it to be a bit bigger and taller.
Only used this tent once so far, but it was easy to put up and a decent size. Wish it was taller, but I knew that before I bought it.

We love the tent, however one of the big tent poles broke the one time we used it. The rubber connect inside of it snapped. Never had that happen before. Disappointed! Smaller than expected
Tent worked well for Florida summer. Did not have rain or wind so cannot attest water or wind proof/resistance.Cheap unusable stakes hence 4 stars.

Have had the coleman sundome 6 person tent out 4 times now on weekend camping trips. Tent sets up well seems very sturdy. Great tent used once for college son to experience outdoors camping. It was easy to setup and seems durable.

easy to set up & downworth the money
Great tent. Took to Dale Hollow. Held up good during a very windy day. Stayed dry during a night of thunderstorms. However, a section of one of the tent poles split.

Easy to assemble. Can't comment on the durability to moisture. As an experienced tenter I always tarp my tents. There are zero tents that can withstand 8 hours of rain two days in a row. The windows don't open to the floor. Door easily opened and closed. It's great for a few days.

Used a couple times, rainfly worked great in the rain.If you are squeezing 4 people in here, you are sleeping shoulder to shoulder lol. For two people, this is fine, but could even be a bit bigger imo. One queen air mattress takes up the entire tent for reference.

So far seems very water resistant like people said. It's roomier inside than you would think. My only reluctance in a five star rating - it is difficult to put up by yourself due to the length of the fiberglass poles. But, one backyard camp out and one camping trip to our favorite campground, seems like a great tent. Looking forward to lots more camping adventures with the tent.

my very first tent and bought 2 person tent definitely not meant for 2 people it was just enough room for myself. I camp a lot, and without a doubt Coleman makes the BEST inexpensive tents. They are light years better than any other brand at a similar price point. My only complaint: like I said, I got this to replace another Coleman 4-man dome tent, so seemingly the exact same tent. Except it's not. It's so much smaller. For one thing, The ceiling is much lower. This means not only can I not stand up in the middle, (which is no big deal,) but the walls are also much more slanted, making the space inside less usable and sort of wasted. My rule of thumb is usually that if you use air mattresses a tent is comfortable for half the amount of people it's advertised for, (so an 8 man comfortable for 4, a 6 man comfortable for 3, etc,) but this 4-man tent is really only about right for 1 person on a single air mattress and their gear. You would have a really hard time trying to put a queen air mattress in it. As long as you are aware of that though, it is an excellent little tent, and an especially great option for beginners because of the simplicity of set-up.

Just received my Posture Corrector and am wearing it as I write this review. First off - it does nothing in the way to physically deterring you from hunching or slumping over your shoulders and back. It digs/cuts into your armpits, especially when you don't wear a short or long sleeve shirt under it (I'm wearing a tank top at the moment).  And, it's difficult to reach the Velcro all the way back to secure it in place without help - but I managed. Maybe if you had a partner who could help you and pull it all the way as far back as it allows it may be different - but I don't think so. There's no "pain relief" about this - it's pain infliction. No wonder they tell you to only wear it for short intervals. I've only had it on for 30 min and have deep red marks where the Velcro straps are digging into my armpits And I'm a very small person with very little fat. You may think - "Oh, that's why then - I have wayyyy more fat than her and therefore it won't bother me as much...more cushion". Again, I don't think so. I have nothing to compare this to as this is the first of this kind I've tried. Could I send it back, get my $$ and buy something comparable instead? Yes, probably. But, I'm pretty sure they will all be like this or similar. And, I need something, anything to stop my friends from asking me to stop slumping, like they're my mom! On my birthday no less, after I put make-up on and a skirt no less! And, there's the fact that I hate to waste anything.
